points.title: 早年教育
points.description: 伏尔泰出生于巴黎一个富裕的中产阶级家庭，原名弗朗索瓦-马里·阿鲁埃。他在耶稣会学校路易大帝学院接受教育，展现出非凡的文学才华。这一时期，他开始接触古典文学和哲学，培养了批判性思维。1711年，他离开学校，决心投身文学创作，但与父亲的关系紧张，父亲希望他成为律师而非作家。这段经历奠定了他日后反抗权威、追求自由的思想基础。
points.descriptionEn: Voltaire was born in Paris to a wealthy middle-class family, originally named François-Marie Arouet. He received his education at the Jesuit school Louis-le-Grand, where he demonstrated exceptional literary talent. During this period, he was exposed to classical literature and philosophy, developing critical thinking skills. In 1711, he left school determined to pursue a literary career, though this strained his relationship with his father, who wanted him to become a lawyer rather than a writer. This experience laid the foundation for his later resistance to authority and pursuit of freedom.

points.title: 文学生涯起步
points.description: 1717年，伏尔泰因讽刺贵族而首次被捕入狱，在巴士底狱度过近一年。出狱后，他创作了悲剧《俄狄浦斯》并获得巨大成功，确立了他在文学界的地位。然而，1726年，他与贵族骑士肖瓦洛发生冲突，再次被迫离开巴黎。这一时期，他创作了大量讽刺作品和诗歌，展现了他对法国社会不公的批判。他的作品风格犀利，语言幽默，但常常触怒权贵，导致他多次被迫流亡。
points.descriptionEn: In 1717, Voltaire was first imprisoned in the Bastille for nearly a year after satirizing an aristocrat. Upon release, he wrote the tragedy 'Oedipus' which achieved great success, establishing his position in literary circles. However, in 1726, he had a conflict with the Chevalier de Rohan and was forced to leave Paris again. During this period, he wrote numerous satirical works and poems, demonstrating his criticism of French social injustice. His writing style was sharp and humorous, but often offended the powerful, leading to multiple exiles.

points.title: 英国启蒙之旅
points.description: 1726年，伏尔泰流亡英国，在那里度过了近三年时间。这段经历对他思想产生了深远影响。他深入研究了英国的政治制度、科学成就和哲学思想，特别是洛克的经验主义和牛顿的科学理论。在英国，他亲眼见证了相对宽容的政治环境和宗教自由，这与法国的专制形成鲜明对比。1729年返回法国后，他创作了《哲学通信》(Philosophical Letters)，系统介绍了英国的自由思想，这本书后来被法国当局查禁，但成为启蒙运动的重要文献。
points.descriptionEn: In 1726, Voltaire went into exile in England, where he spent nearly three years. This experience profoundly influenced his thinking. He studied British political systems, scientific achievements, and philosophical ideas, particularly Locke's empiricism and Newton's scientific theories. In England, he witnessed the relatively tolerant political environment and religious freedom, which stood in stark contrast to French absolutism. After returning to France in 1729, he wrote 'Letters Concerning the English Nation,' systematically introducing English free-thinking ideas. The book was later banned by French authorities but became an important work of the Enlightenment.

points.title: 腓特烈大帝宫廷
points.description: 1750年，伏尔泰应普鲁士国王腓特烈大帝的邀请前往柏林，担任宫廷哲学家和史官。在普鲁士的三年间，他参与了多项文化项目，包括撰写《路易十四时代》等历史著作。然而，他与腓特烈大帝的关系逐渐恶化，主要源于两人性格差异和哲学分歧。伏尔泰追求思想自由，而腓特烈虽然开明但仍是专制君主。1753年，两人最终决裂，伏尔泰被迫离开普鲁士。这段经历让他更加认识到开明专制的局限性，也促使他进一步发展自己的政治哲学思想。
points.descriptionEn: In 1750, Voltaire was invited to Berlin by King Frederick the Great of Prussia to serve as court philosopher and historiographer. During his three years in Prussia, he participated in various cultural projects, including writing historical works such as 'The Age of Louis XIV.' However, his relationship with Frederick gradually deteriorated due to personality differences and philosophical disagreements. Voltaire valued intellectual freedom, while Frederick, though enlightened, remained an absolute monarch. In 1753, the two finally parted ways, and Voltaire was forced to leave Prussia. This experience made him more aware of the limitations of enlightened absolutism and prompted him to further develop his political philosophy.

points.title: 晚年创作与启蒙
points.description: 1755年，伏尔泰在瑞士与法国边境的小镇费尔奈定居，度过了他生命中最后的23年。在这里，他成为欧洲启蒙运动的中心人物，接待了来自各国的知识分子和政治家。他创作了大量重要作品，包括讽刺小说《老实人》、哲学著作《哲学辞典》和历史著作《路易十五时代》。费尔奈时期，他积极参与社会改革运动，为受迫害的新教徒和卡拉斯案受害者辩护，倡导宗教宽容和司法公正。1778年，伏尔泰在巴黎去世，享年84岁，他的葬礼成为法国人民对启蒙思想的盛大致敬。
points.descriptionEn: In 1755, Voltaire settled in Ferney, a small town on the Swiss-French border, where he spent the last 23 years of his life. Here, he became a central figure of the European Enlightenment, hosting intellectuals and politicians from across Europe. He wrote numerous important works, including the satirical novel 'Candide,' the philosophical 'Philosophical Dictionary,' and the historical 'The Age of Louis XV.' During his Ferney years, he actively participated in social reform movements, defending persecuted Protestants and victims of the Calas affair, advocating religious tolerance and judicial justice. Voltaire died in Paris in 1778 at the age of 84, and his funeral became a grand tribute by the French people to Enlightenment ideas.

appraisal.zh: 伏尔泰通常被看作启蒙运动的旗手，他对言论自由、宗教宽容与理性批判的倡导，以及为卡拉斯案等冤案奔走的人道精神，深刻影响了现代民主观念。不过，也有研究者指出其思想存在明显矛盾：他对犹太人等群体抱有偏见，与专制君主关系密切，所谓开明专制实则维护特权，自然神论也未能完全摆脱宗教观念。这些局限说明，即便是启蒙领袖也难以超越自己的时代。
appraisal.en: Voltaire is generally seen as the standard-bearer of the Enlightenment: his advocacy of free speech, religious tolerance and rational critique, and his humanitarian defense of victims such as the Calas affair, profoundly shaped modern democratic ideas. Yet other scholars note clear contradictions—his prejudices against groups such as Jews, his closeness to absolute monarchs, an 'enlightened absolutism' that in practice upheld privilege, and a deism that never fully escaped religious thinking. Such limits show that even an Enlightenment leader could not rise entirely above his age.

supporter.zh: 伏尔泰被誉为启蒙运动的旗手和导师，他倡导的言论自由、宗教宽容和理性批判精神深刻影响了现代民主制度的发展。他的作品如《哲学通信》和《哲学辞典》传播了科学思想和进步观念，挑战了教会权威和专制统治。伏尔泰为卡拉斯案等冤案辩护，展现了人道主义精神，他的名言'我不同意你的观点，但我誓死捍卫你说话的权利'成为自由主义的经典表述。作为思想解放的先驱，伏尔泰的精神遗产至今仍激励着追求真理和正义的人们。
supporter.en: Voltaire is celebrated as a leader and mentor of the Enlightenment movement. His advocacy for freedom of speech, religious tolerance, and rational critique profoundly influenced the development of modern democratic institutions. Works like his 'Letters Concerning the English Nation' and 'Philosophical Dictionary' disseminated scientific ideas and progressive concepts, challenging ecclesiastical authority and autocratic rule. His defense of victims in cases like the Calas affair demonstrated humanitarian spirit, and his famous quote 'I disapprove of what you say, but I will defend to the death your right to say it' has become a classic expression of liberalism. As a pioneer of intellectual liberation, Voltaire's legacy continues to inspire those who seek truth and justice.

critic.zh: 批评者指出伏尔泰的思想存在明显矛盾，他一方面倡导自由，另一方面却对某些群体持有偏见，如对犹太人的刻板印象和对非欧洲文明的轻视。他的贵族出身和与专制君主的密切关系也引发质疑，有人认为他的'开明专制'理念实质上维护了特权阶级的利益。此外，伏尔泰虽然批判教会，却未能完全摆脱宗教思想的影响，他的自然神论仍保留了某种形式的宗教观念。这些局限性表明，即使是启蒙运动的领袖，也难以完全摆脱所处时代的历史局限。
critic.en: Critics point out that Voltaire's思想 contained significant contradictions. While advocating for freedom, he held prejudices against certain groups, such as stereotypes about Jews and dismissive attitudes toward non-European civilizations. His aristocratic background and close relationships with absolute monarchs have also been questioned, with some arguing that his concept of 'enlightened absolutism' essentially upheld the interests of privileged classes. Furthermore, although he criticized the church, Voltaire未能完全摆脱 religious influence, as his deism retained certain forms of religious belief. These limitations suggest that even leaders of the Enlightenment could not entirely escape the historical constraints of their time.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，伏尔泰常被塑造为启蒙运动的象征性人物，代表着理性、批判精神和反抗权威的勇气。他的生平和作品被广泛研究，成为理解18世纪欧洲思想变革的关键。伏尔泰的形象既有历史真实性也有被神话的成分，他既是一位多产的作家和思想家，也是一位善于自我宣传的公众人物。现代学术界更倾向于将他置于更复杂的历史语境中，既肯定他对自由、宽容和人道主义的贡献，也认识到其思想的历史局限性。伏尔泰的名字已成为启蒙精神的代名词，在全球范围内持续影响着人们对自由、理性和正义的追求。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Voltaire is often portrayed as a symbolic figure of the Enlightenment, representing reason, critical spirit, and courage in challenging authority. His life and works are widely studied as key to understanding the intellectual transformations of 18th-century Europe. Voltaire's image contains both historical authenticity and mythologized elements; he was both a prolific writer and thinker and a master of self-promotion. Modern scholarship tends to place him in a more complex historical context, acknowledging both his contributions to freedom, tolerance, and humanitarianism, and recognizing the limitations of his thought. Voltaire's name has become synonymous with the Enlightenment spirit, continuing to influence global pursuits of freedom, reason, and justice.

self.zh: 我不同意你的观点，但我誓死捍卫你说话的权利。
self.en: I disapprove of what you say, but I will defend to the death your right to say it.
